subject: Pricing mapping for AWS/GCP/Azure private offers & $/1M token targets
messages:
From: John Lee <john.lee@skyline.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intro + marketplace procurement questions

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap from our side and a few specific asks so we can move to procurement.

Summary of Skyline needs:
- Estimated monthly token volume: 20M - 30M tokens/month initially, scaling to 100M+ in Q4 if pilot performs well.
- Primary use: chat generation (customer support) + embedding indexing for semantic search (embedding volume ~10% of gen tokens).
- Budget range we can entertain for committed usage: target around $8-$12 per 1M tokens (this is our target delivered to finance).

Questions we need answered for procurement/marketplace team:
1) How do Redwood hosted list prices map to private offers in AWS/GCP/Azure marketplaces?
2) What does a $/1M token unit price look like after marketplace fees / commissions?
3) Can you provide example math for our expected volumes (20M / month) showing final $/1M delivered to Skyline if we use a marketplace private offer vs direct contract?

If you can send a simple worksheet with the mapping and assumptions (marketplace fee %, taxes, any reseller margins) that would be perfect — our procurement wants that to evaluate the PO.

Thanks,
John
John Lee
Head of Platform
Skyline Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: John Lee <john.lee@skyline.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + marketplace procurement questions

John — thanks for the clear recap and the target range. Attaching a first-pass worksheet that maps list vs private-offer math across marketplaces (see attachment). High-level notes below + next steps.

High-level:
- Redwood hosted list price (example): $12 / 1M tokens (chat model family on standard config).
- Customer target: you mentioned $8-$12 / 1M — to be concrete, tell us your preferred target inside that range (we can plan commit tiers).
- Marketplace private offers: typically we publish a list price on the marketplace then create a private offer which applies a negotiated price to your account. Marketplace fees / charges vary by provider — we show an illustrative % in the worksheet.

Example assumptions in the worksheet (tab "Assumptions"):
- AWS Marketplace fee: 8% (placeholder, confirm with AWS rep)
- GCP Marketplace fee: 8%
- Azure Marketplace fee: 10%
- Taxes and VAT not included (we call out how they flow)

Example math (from worksheet):
- Hosted list: $12 / 1M
- To deliver a customer-facing $9 / 1M after an 8% marketplace fee, the private-offer listing price needs to be $9 / (1 - 0.08) = $9.78 -> round to $9.80.
- For committed 20M tokens/month that equates to approx $180/month vs list $240 (illustrative).

Action items / next steps:
1) Confirm which marketplace you will use (AWS/GCP/Azure).
2) Confirm target $/1M delivered to Skyline (pick single number e.g. $10/1M).
3) We will: (a) send a clean pricing worksheet with marketplace fee assumptions, (b) loop in the marketplace rep for private-offer flow, and (c) draft a mutual action plan with procurement dates.

Attachment: 2026-02-25_redwood_marketplace_pricing_mapping.xlsx

Thanks — I can jump on a 30-min follow-up next week if useful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0124
From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@amazon.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, John Lee <john.lee@skyline.ai>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing mapping for AWS/GCP/Azure private offers & $/1M token targets

Thanks for the ping — happy to help clarify AWS Marketplace private offer flow. A couple quick points and a short PDF attached.

- Private offer price: when you create a private offer, the negotiated price replaces the list price for that buyer account. The buyer sees the private offer price in the invoice.
- Marketplace fees: vary by product type and contract; for SaaS/usage-based we typically operate in the 5-12% band depending on distribution agreements. We recommend using a conservative 8% for initial modeling.
- Billing showback: AWS invoices can show the marketplace line item and we can include charge detail for token usage if you publish usage dimensions.

I'll connect your deals team with a marketplace specialist who can run the exact fee schedule for your SKU.

Attachment: AWS_private_offer_flow.pdf

Best,
Priya Singh
AWS Marketplace Sales
priya.singh@amazon.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, John Lee <john.lee@skyline.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Mar 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing mapping for AWS/GCP/Azure private offers & $/1M token targets

John / team — quick internal math validation and recommended ask to procurement.

Assumptions (illustrative):
- Redwood hosted list: $12 / 1M tokens
- Target customer delivered price: $10 / 1M (example)
- Marketplace fee: 8%

Calculation:
- Required private-offer listing price = target / (1 - fee) = $10 / 0.92 = $10.87 -> round to $10.90
- At 20M tokens/month, delivered cost to customer = 20 * $10 = $200.
- Compare to hosted list: 20 * $12 = $240. So customer sees $40 improvement/month versus list in this scenario.

Notes for procurement worksheet: include both per-1M math and total monthly commitment line items; show sensitivity for 10% and 5% marketplace fees.

Marissa — if Skyline confirms $10/1M delivered and AWS as the marketplace, we should: 1) prepare private-offer worksheet with exact fee bands, 2) draft the private offer and 3) share a one-page mutual action plan for procurement (PO dates, POC window, billing contacts).

Aditya
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
From: John Lee <john.lee@skyline.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@amazon.com>

Subject: Re: Pricing mapping for AWS/GCP/Azure private offers & $/1M token targets

Thanks everyone — helpful.

Skyline confirmation: we want to target a delivered price of $10 / 1M tokens for a committed 20M tokens/month pilot (3-month PO to start).

Procurement asks:
- Can Redwood send the finalized pricing worksheet with the private-offer listing price (we need that for our PO).
- Can AWS confirm the expected fee % for Redwood's SKU (Priya?) so we can show net delivered price to finance.
- Timeline: procurement aims to issue a PO by 2026-03-10 if we have the worksheet and private offer draft by 2026-03-05.

If you can send the one-pager mutual action plan and the worksheet today/tomorrow, we'll review and route to procurement. Happy to hop on a short call if needed.

Regards,
John
